newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds, futures seen taking lead from U.S..
newsitem.headline: German Bunds, futures seen taking lead from U.S..

text.p: German Bunds and futures climbed confidently on Monday, recouping most of the ground lost on Friday and with encouragement coming from a recovery in the U.S. debt market.

Dealers said comments by White House chief economist Joseph Stiglitz that he had no worries about inflation had helped boost bond markets, but said the lack of other fundamental news had led to the market to rely on technical signals.
"We don't have any strength of our own," said one dealer, adding that a similar development could be expected on Tuesday.
March Bund futures were up 72 basis points at 100.79, while the 10-year Bund rose to 103.42, yielding 5.56 percent.

Earlier in the day the March future broke through critical resistance around 100.55 points, which sparked some technical buying. Chartists said next resistance came in at 100.84 and 101.11, with support at 100.62 and 100.30 points.

Dealers said the market had been reassured by comments from the meeting of the Group of 10 central banks that global financial markets had over-reacted last week to comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, about "irrational exuberance" in asset markets.
